impact: matrix.mjs publishes a generation of five evidence files by renaming five staged files into place one at a time. A crash between renames leaves a mixed generation: some files from this run, some from the last. The attempt marker covers the window (verify-evidence.mjs refuses while it is present, and it is removed only after the final rename), so nothing consumes the mixture — but that is a refusal, not atomicity, and it means an interrupted run leaves the working tree needing a full re-run rather than a clean rollback. Review round 2 chunk 13 added the missing parts that were cheap and local: the staged files are now read back and re-parsed before any rename, each is fsynced, and the directory is fsynced after the renames and again after the marker is removed. What remains is the transaction boundary itself: publish into a generation-specific directory and switch one pointer, so the whole generation becomes visible in a single durable operation. This is the same boundary as ISS-049 (receipt publication is two renames) and ISS-052 (the decision document, the machine record and the attempt-report removal are three effects). All three want doing together — a shared durable-publish helper — rather than three separate patches, which is why this is filed rather than fixed inside a review round.
title: Evidence publication has no single commit point — five renames are five effects
